top_choice_rationale: Ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed C-N coupling by Buchwald and Hartwig is a general method, about thirty years mature and the default route to aryl amines in medicinal and process chemistry. It solves a distinct mechanistic problem from the 2010 C-C coupling prize: binding and deprotonating a coordinating amine and forcing a slow C-N reductive elimination against beta-hydride elimination. The attribution to two originators who worked in parallel is clean and the citation scope is a single coherent achievement. P001 is a clear second: a new mode of action with independent confirmation, though no approved degrader yet and the Handa/Ito cereblon strand left out. P002 ranks third because it joins two unrelated achievements, and the base editing part is the less mature and sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize. No award is last since several achievements are ripe.
